analysis_summaries: The repository provides checkout-lane monitoring using a COCO-pretrained YOLO11s person detector. It accepts image or multi-frame input, preprocesses frames as RGB 640×640 letterboxed tensors scaled to [0,1], and runs the local ONNX model. Its decoder transposes the raw predictions, applies confidence filtering and NMS, and returns image-coordinate detection boxes. Optional cashier and queue polygons support lane-status logic; the scan does not verify recall under severe crowd occlusion.

info.user_prompt: Detect and track every person in a dense crowd seen from a fixed, elevated camera. Input: the video file /home/dread/videos/crowd/MOT20-02.mp4 for now (later a USB camera or an RTSP stream). Model: a person or head detector that works under heavy occlusion, small enough for a GeForce GTX 1650 with 4 GB (batch 1, about 640 px input), compiled to a TensorRT FP16 engine (INT8 as well if possible, for comparison), with the speed report. Tracking: multi-object tracking with persistent IDs (DeepStream nvtracker). Output: for every frame, JSON metadata with each person's bounding box in pixels, tracker ID, confidence and the frame timestamp, written to a JSON file and also published over MQTT on topic crowdshield/detections to broker localhost:1883. Show the video with boxes and IDs. Do not store video or faces.
